lesson.title: NDP: IPv6's Neighbor Discovery Protocol
lesson.summary: NDP performs the same address resolution job ARP performs for IPv4, along with router and configuration discovery, but it does so using ICMPv6 messages sent to efficient multicast addresses instead of a separate broadcast protocol.
lesson.body:
IPv6 does not use ARP. When its designers rebuilt the protocol suite, they folded address resolution into ICMPv6 itself, producing a broader toolset called the Neighbor Discovery Protocol, or NDP. NDP does everything ARP used to do for finding a neighbor's MAC address, and it also takes on jobs that IPv4 networks handled through entirely separate mechanisms, such as discovering a default router and configuring an address automatically.

The core resolution exchange in NDP mirrors ARP's request and reply, but with different names and a different delivery method. Where ARP broadcasts a request to every device on the network, NDP sends a Neighbor Solicitation message to a solicited node multicast address computed from the target's IP address, so that in practice only the handful of devices whose addresses share the same trailing bits, usually just the intended target, even receive the message, rather than flooding the entire local network the way an ARP broadcast does. The device that owns the target address responds with a Neighbor Advertisement, the counterpart to an ARP reply, which carries its link layer MAC address back to the requester.

Picture the same scenario as the ARP chapter, translated into IPv6. A host needs the MAC address behind a neighbor's IPv6 address to build a frame. Instead of broadcasting, it computes the solicited node multicast address that corresponds to the last twenty four bits of the target's address and sends a Neighbor Solicitation there. The owner of that address recognizes the solicitation, and answers with a Neighbor Advertisement containing its own MAC address, which the requester then caches, exactly as an ARP cache entry would be cached, so that future frames to that neighbor do not require the exchange to repeat.

NDP goes further than ARP ever did. Router Solicitation and Router Advertisement messages let a host discover its default gateway and learn the network prefix in use on the link without any manual configuration or a separate protocol like DHCP, a process that underlies stateless address autoconfiguration. NDP also includes Duplicate Address Detection, in which a host uses a Neighbor Solicitation for its own prospective address before actually using it, to confirm that no other device on the link already holds it. The unifying idea across all of this is that IPv6 consolidated address resolution and several other IPv4 side protocols into one coherent set of ICMPv6 based messages, rather than relying on ARP's separate, broadcast heavy, Ethernet specific mechanism.
